about: CHAIN black_stones (Design/content/CHAINS.md; page Design/content/chains/black_stones.md; words Data/writing/chain_black_stones.json). The quarrel of King Charles and King Offa that shut the ports about 789-790, and the letter of 796 about black stones and the length of cloaks: a Frisian of Dorestad caught between two kings. Fourteen cards, 793 to 796 (endings may be collected to 799). The spine's thread black_stones: its flags bs_ban_heard, bs_letter and bs_peace are set here where a step is also the thread's step. Step flags ch_black_stones_1 .. _10; endings ch_black_stones_end_early (history changed: changed_offa_peace_early), ch_black_stones_end_peace (what happened), ch_black_stones_end_shut (history changed: changed_offa_letter_lost), ch_black_stones_end_runner. Every option's note names its outcome text. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start (drawn at Dorestad before 796). Quernstones finished for the English trade lie unsold; the skippers argue whether the king's order binds Frisians. Sources: Gesta abbatum Fontanellensium c. 12 (the order that no one from Britain and the English people should touch the shore of Gaul to trade); Alcuin to Colcu, 790 (MGH Epistolae IV no. 7: sailing forbidden to merchants on both sides); Dorestad's quern cutters finishing Mayen roughouts (dossiers/dorestad.md). Whether the order bound Frisians is not recorded (?). Cast: cast.thiadbod; the cutter Folkmar is invented (Folc- + -mar). Sets ch_black_stones_1 and, on trust, ch_black_stones_trust.

The West Saxon wic stays half open; Thiadbod's man sends English cloaks over as pilgrims' bundles. Sources: Beorhtric of Wessex married Offa's daughter Eadburh (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 787 for 789); how far the ban reached is not recorded (spine: the game lets Hamwic stay half open) (?); traders hiding among pilgrims are in Charles's letter of 796 (MGH Epistolae IV no. 100; Giles 1847 from William of Malmesbury). Cast: cast.thiadbod's man Hildulf, invented (Hild- + -ulf). Sets ch_black_stones_3h; ch_black_stones_runner if the cloth is run; ch_black_stones_watched if it is caught.

cards.note: Step 4 (scheduled 25 days after step 2, or 40 by the road round, at Lundenwic). The reeve wants a quiet ship to take a letter to Gervold's clerk at Quentovic, and a rod cut to the length of the stones his king wants. Sources: Gervold was Offa's friend, Offa's letters to him lay at Saint-Wandrille, and he went to Offa many times as the king's envoy (Gesta abbatum Fontanellensium c. 12); Offa 'made known his wish about the length of the stones' (Charles to Offa, 796, MGH Epistolae IV no. 100, our rendering). That the length went as a rod, and that a reeve wrote, are ours (?). Cast: cast.wighelm, cast.gervold. Sets ch_black_stones_4; carrying sets the spine's bs_letter and ch_black_stones_rod; refusing sets ch_black_stones_refused and ch_black_stones_runner.

cards.note: Step 5, optional (drawn at sea while the letter is aboard). A Frankish king's boat in the Channel asks whose cloth that is. Sources: the spine's sea hook for the thread; coast guards and ships against the Northmen are ordered by Charles only from 800 (Annales regni Francorum 800), so a king's boat in 793-796 is the toll-gatherer's own, which is ours (?). The order in the officer's mouth is the Gesta's, our rendering. Sets ch_black_stones_hailed; ch_black_stones_seal_shown, or ch_black_stones_letter_taken if she runs and is caught.

cards.note: Step 6 (scheduled by step 4; the first call at Quentovic after it). Gervold's toll house: his clerk takes the letter and the rod; an English ship lies under arrest. Sources: Gervold 'for many years procurator over the kingdom's trade, collecting tributes and tolls in divers ports and cities, chiefly at Quentawich' (Gesta abbatum Fontanellensium c. 12, the spine's rendering); he roofed Saint Peter's and Saint Michael's with lead (same chapter); English lead as the likely source (?). The arrested ship is the spine's hook; her master Hunberht is invented (Hun- + -berht). Sets ch_black_stones_6, clears bs_letter; ch_black_stones_ship_freed, or ch_black_stones_read with ch_black_stones_seal_seen.

cards.note: Step 7 (scheduled 20 days after step 6, at Rotomagus). Saint-Wandrille, Gervold's own house, lies down the Seine: Offa's letters are in its chest, and a monk says what the quarrel was about. Sources: Gesta abbatum Fontanellensium c. 12: the younger Charles asked for Offa's daughter; Offa would not agree unless Bertha, Charles's daughter, were given to his son; the king, 'somewhat moved' (aliquantulum commotus, our rendering), gave the order; Offa's letters to Gervold still lay at the abbey. Charles asks that the cloaks be made as they used to come (MGH Epistolae IV no. 100); that the old length went as a knotted cord is ours (?). The monk's complaint of the cold is the scribes' own (marginal notes of the period). Cast: cast.gervold, cast.sigewine. Sets ch_black_stones_7, ch_black_stones_cord and the spine's bs_letter.

cards.note: ENDING: the early peace, the hard road, HISTORY CHANGED (drawn at Lundenwic from the Easter after the abbot's embassy, 794 to early 796). Flags ch_black_stones_end_early, changed_offa_peace_early, bs_peace. Grand rewards: unlock_title_two_kings_merchant with one of unlock_charter_lundenwic, unlock_factor_quentovic, unlock_plot_lundenwic. What really happened: the peace is known only from Charles's letter of 796 (MGH Epistolae IV no. 100), in which each king's merchants have the other's protection and may appeal to the king; Gervold went to Offa many times as envoy (Gesta c. 12). Here it comes a year or two sooner, by a rod, a cord and eight pigs of lead. A Frisian toll-free at Lundenwic by a king's writing is modelled on the later toll charters of English kings for ships at Lundenwic (Aethelbald for the bishops of Rochester and Worcester and for Minster in Thanet, 730s-740s) (?). Cast: cast.wighelm, cast.gervold.

cards.note: ENDING: the peace of 796, WHAT REALLY HAPPENED (drawn at Lundenwic from May 796 for anyone who heard the ban and neither sold the answer nor refused the letter). Flags ch_black_stones_end_peace, bs_peace. Grand rewards: unlock_charter_lundenwic for the carrier of the answer; with unlock_factor_quentovic for one who also landed the lead (the hard road, when the early peace was missed); unlock_pilot_thames for anyone. Sources: Charles to Offa, 796 (MGH Epistolae IV no. 100; in part in William of Malmesbury, tr. J. A. Giles 1847). Quoted from Giles in reeve_letter and reeve_gifts: 'go peaceably without any molestation', 'not seeking the cause of religion, but that of gain', 'pay the customary tolls in proper places', 'a belt, an Hungarian sword, and two silk cloaks'; the stones and cloaks are our own rendering. Offa died 29 July 796, three days before Lammas; his son Ecgfrith reigned 141 days (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 794 for 796). Cast: cast.wighelm.

cards.note: ENDING: the answer sold, HISTORY CHANGED (drawn at Hamwic from Lammas 796 for one who sold the abbot's answer at step 9). Flags ch_black_stones_end_shut, changed_offa_letter_lost; lasting cost ch_black_stones_abbot_remembers unless the player owns up. Grand rewards: unlock_factor_hamwic or unlock_pilot_solent. What really happened: the letter of 796 was written and Offa died on 29 July with the quarrel mended. Here no answer reached him: the letter about black stones is never written, he dies unreconciled, and the ports stay shut under Coenwulf, who has Kent's rising on his hands (Eadberht Praen, 796-798: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle). The engine's card long.offa_letter.796 must not fire when changed_offa_letter_lost is set (see 'needs' in the chain page). Cast: cast.thiadbod and his man Hildulf (invented).
